192769622.title: File:Western Tree Frog the rain-born climber hidden within the emerald forests of the Western Ghats 01.jpg

ImageDescription.value:
The Western Tree Frog is a rare and fascinating amphibian endemic to the Western Ghats of India. This beautiful tree frog was scientifically recorded from the western mountain forests of India, particularly across parts of Maharashtra, Goa, Karnataka, Kerala, and Tamil Nadu within moist evergreen ecosystems. It survives mainly in forested hill regions rich in rainfall and dense vegetation.

The frog is admired for its elegant slender body, smooth skin texture, and earthy coloration that ranges from light brown and olive to greenish shades with darker irregular markings. Its delicate body patterns help it blend perfectly with wet tree bark, leaves, and forest vegetation. Large golden eyes and long adhesive toe pads make it a skilled climber among branches and shrubs.

This species is famous for its secretive and seasonal behavior. It is mostly active during monsoon and humid nights when forests become alive with amphibian activity. Outside the rainy season, sightings become extremely rare as the frog hides deep within vegetation and moist tree hollows.

Insectivorous by nature, it feeds mainly on moths, beetles, termites, ants, spiders, and other small forest insects. The species inhabits evergreen forests, plantations, streamsides, forest edges, and dense canopy vegetation where humidity remains high.

Like many Western Ghats amphibians, the Western Tree Frog plays an important ecological role by naturally controlling insect populations. Its soft breeding calls echo through rain-soaked forests during the monsoon, making it one of the hidden nocturnal voices of India’s ancient mountain wilderness.

Photographed in Munnar, Kerala, India
